belief: My body and its desires are shameful.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your body and its desires are shameful, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being shamed as a child about your body, appearance, or normal curiosity. Teaching that treated the body as evil and only the soul as good. Silence or embarrassment about sex, hunger, rest, or pleasure. Past abuse or misuse that left you feeling dirty. Cultural messages that criticize your shape, size, or looks.
teaches: God created the human body and called it very good. You are fearfully and wonderfully made. Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, bought at a price, and meant to glorify God. Natural desires such as hunger, rest, and closeness are gifts from God, to be received with thanksgiving and guided by His Word. Sin can misuse good desires, but the body and its God-given desires are not shameful in themselves.
self_statements: My body is something to be ashamed of.
God only cares about my soul.
I hate the way I was made.
I need to punish or ignore my body.
errors: Believing the body is either perfect or entirely shameful.
Treating all desire as sinful because some desires can be misused.
Concluding “I feel ashamed, so my body must be shameful.”
Overlooking what God says about how He made you.
questions: What did God say about His creation, including the human body?
If I am fearfully and wonderfully made, who taught me to be ashamed?
Is my body a temple to be honored or a prison to be punished?
Can a desire be good while still needing God’s guidance?
Does Scripture say to reject God’s good gifts or receive them with thanks?
Am I confusing what was done to me with who I am?
How would I treat my body if I saw it as God’s temple?
truth: My body is not shameful. God made it, called it very good, and made me fearfully and wonderfully. My body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. My natural desires are gifts from God, to be received with thanks and guided by His Word. I can honor God with my body instead of being ashamed of it.
hw_questions: What did God say about the body He made?
Who taught me to be ashamed of my body?
Is my body a temple or a prison?
Can a desire be good and still need guidance?
Does God want me to reject His gifts or give thanks?
How would I treat a temple of the Holy Spirit?
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
God called the body He made very good.
My body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.
My natural desires are gifts to be guided, not shamed.
I can honor God with my body.
What God created, I can receive with thanks.
log: Each day, thank God for one thing my body did for me, such as walking, hugging, tasting, or healing.
name_example: I praise You, for Sarah is fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.
actions: Stand in front of a mirror and read Psalm 139:13–16 aloud,
then name one part of your body you can thank God for.
Do one kind thing for your body this week,
such as rest, a healthy meal, or a walk, as an act of honoring God.
Write down one shaming message about your body
you heard growing up, and next to it write what God says.
Talk with a counselor or trusted believer
if past hurt has made your body feel dirty.
tracker: One thing my body did that I’m thankful for
prayer: Creator God, thank You for making me fearfully and wonderfully. Help me reject the lie that my body and its desires are shameful. Teach me to see my body as Your temple, to receive Your good gifts with thanks, and to honor You with how I live. Heal any shame others placed on me. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
